source_system_summary.processing_description: Weekly maintenance of the transaction-type reference table from an A/U/D file.

steps: STEP1 IKJEFT01: DSN RUN PROGRAM(COBTUPDT) PLAN(CARDDEMO)

business_rules.statement: OPEN FILE OK / NOT OK is displayed and the read loop runs either way (0001-OPEN-FILES falls through).
Record type A inserts, U updates, D deletes, '*' is a comment; any other type is an error.
INSERT/UPDATE bind the 2-character type code and the full 50-character description (trailing spaces stored).
SQLCODE +100 on UPDATE/DELETE would report 'No records found.', but Open COBOL ESQL returns 0 when no row matches, so a missing row reports success (fixture t05).
An error DISPLAYs WS-RETURN-MSG (never cleared), sets RETURN-CODE 4 and processing continues with the next record.
Negative SQLCODE message: 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:' followed by SQLCODE edited ----9.

gaps.description: Plugin numeric convention prescribes MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero; the legacy source has no ROUNDED and golden fixtures prove truncation (i02-tie-half-cent). Legacy truncation is kept (ADR-003).

SQLCODEs come from Open COBOL ESQL over PostgreSQL, not Db2: unique violation -403, any other error -400, no row found 0 (+100 never raised). Under PostgreSQL a failed statement aborts the whole unit of work (d03: COBTUPDT's later UPDATE also fails); Db2 would roll back only the failed statement. The port reproduces the golden (PostgreSQL) behaviour; a savepoint-per-statement policy is a migration decision (ADR-007).
